title: Throughput value in an alert email is converted, not raw bps

steps.action: Login as admin; create a metric alert policy on a network throughput counter with an email notification, then breach it at roughly 21890802 bps
steps.expected: Alert fires and the email is delivered

steps.action: Read the metric value in the email
steps.expected: It reads as a converted unit (e.g. 20.88 Mbps), not the raw 21890802. This is the reported defect

title: Email value matches what the UI shows for the same alert

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy and open the resulting alert in Active Alerts
steps.expected: Alert detail shows the converted value

steps.action: Compare against the email for the same alert
steps.expected: Value, unit and precision are identical. The ticket requires the email to reuse the UI/Reports conversion logic, not a second implementation

title: Email value matches what a report shows for the same interval

steps.action: Run a report covering the breach interval for the same counter
steps.expected: Report renders the converted value

steps.action: Compare against the email
steps.expected: Identical value, unit and precision across UI, report and email

title: Throughput converts from bps to Kbps at the boundary

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at a value around 1500 bps
steps.expected: Alert email is delivered

steps.action: Read the value and unit in the email
steps.expected: It is expressed in Kbps with the numeric value scaled accordingly, matching the UI for the same input

title: Throughput converts from Kbps to Mbps at the boundary

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at a value around 2500 Kbps
steps.expected: Alert email is delivered

steps.action: Read the value and unit in the email
steps.expected: It is expressed in Mbps with the numeric value scaled accordingly, matching the UI for the same input

title: Throughput converts from Mbps to Gbps at the boundary

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at a value around 4096 Mbps
steps.expected: Alert email is delivered

steps.action: Read the value and unit in the email
steps.expected: It is expressed in Gbps with the numeric value scaled accordingly, matching the UI for the same input

title: Throughput converts from Gbps to Tbps at the boundary

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at a value around 2048 Gbps
steps.expected: Alert email is delivered

steps.action: Read the value and unit in the email
steps.expected: It is expressed in Tbps with the numeric value scaled accordingly, matching the UI for the same input

title: Converted value always carries its unit

steps.action: Breach policies on several convertible counters and collect the emails
steps.expected: Emails delivered

steps.action: Inspect each metric value
steps.expected: Every converted value shows both the number and its unit — never a bare number whose scale the reader has to guess

title: Byte/storage counters are converted in email

steps.action: Breach a policy on a disk or memory counter reported in bytes
steps.expected: Alert email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Expressed in the appropriate KB/MB/GB/TB unit, matching the UI

title: Time/duration counters are converted in email

steps.action: Breach a policy on a counter reported in milliseconds or seconds
steps.expected: Alert email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Expressed in the unit the UI uses for that counter with matching precision

title: Percentage counters are not double-converted

steps.action: Breach a policy on a CPU or memory percentage counter
steps.expected: Alert email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Shown as a percentage exactly as the UI shows it — not rescaled or given a throughput unit

title: Unitless counters are unchanged

steps.action: Breach a policy on a unitless counter such as a session or error count
steps.expected: Alert email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Rendered as the plain number with no invented unit

title: Zero and very small values render sensibly

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at 0 bps, then at 1 bps
steps.expected: Both emails delivered

steps.action: Read both values
steps.expected: Rendered as 0 bps and 1 bps in the base unit — not as 0.000001 Mbps or an empty value

title: Very large values scale to the top unit without overflow

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy at a value in the Tbps range
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Scaled to the highest supported unit, readable, with no scientific notation or truncation

title: Negative or invalid metric values do not break the template

steps.action: Force an alert whose metric value is negative or null
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Inspect the email
steps.expected: The template renders a safe placeholder and still delivers; it does not fail to send or print a stack trace

title: Decimal precision matches the UI rather than being rounded away

steps.action: Breach a policy at a value with meaningful decimals (e.g. 20.88 Mbps)
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Compare the decimals against the UI
steps.expected: Same number of decimal places; the conversion precision must match existing UI/Reports behaviour

title: Scope is metric notifications only, as implemented

steps.action: Trigger an availability/service-check alert email and a metric alert email
steps.expected: Both delivered

steps.action: Compare the value rendering
steps.expected: Conversion applies to metric-related notification data. The dev comment on the ticket limits the delivered scope to metric notifications — confirm any non-metric template is intentionally unchanged rather than silently missed

title: Teams and Slack channels are consistent with email or explicitly out of scope

steps.action: Configure a policy to notify by email, Microsoft Teams and Slack, then breach it
steps.expected: All three notifications are delivered

steps.action: Compare the metric value across channels
steps.expected: Either all three show the converted value, or the ticket's stated backend-conversion intent is not yet met for the other channels — the reviewer comment warns that email-only conversion creates exactly this inconsistency

title: Alert email macros other than the metric value are unaffected

steps.action: Breach a policy whose email template uses monitor name, severity, timestamp and policy name macros
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Inspect every macro
steps.expected: All resolve as before; only the metric value rendering changed

title: A custom email template picks up conversion too

steps.action: Customise the alert email template for a policy, keeping the metric value macro, then breach it
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Read the value
steps.expected: Converted the same way as the default template — conversion lives in the value rendering, not in one hard-coded template

title: Clear/recovery email uses the same conversion

steps.action: Breach a throughput policy then let it recover so a clear email is sent
steps.expected: Both emails delivered

steps.action: Compare value rendering in the breach and clear emails
steps.expected: Both converted identically

title: No conversion is applied twice on a re-notified alert

steps.action: Configure repeat notification on a breached policy and let it re-notify several times
steps.expected: Multiple emails delivered

steps.action: Compare the values
steps.expected: Every email shows the same converted value — the number is not rescaled again on each send

title: XSS/injection through a metric or monitor name in email is neutralised

steps.action: Name a monitor <script>alert(1)</script> and breach a policy on it so an email is sent
steps.expected: Email delivered

steps.action: Open the email in an HTML-rendering client
steps.expected: The name is escaped as literal text; no script or remote content executes from the template

title: Existing alerts and history are not rewritten

steps.action: Note the stored raw values for alerts raised before the change
steps.expected: Baseline captured

steps.action: Re-inspect after the change
steps.expected: Stored data is untouched — conversion happens at render time only, so historical accuracy and any downstream integration consuming raw values are preserved

title: Email rendering does not measurably slow notification delivery

steps.action: Breach 50 policies with email notification simultaneously
steps.expected: All emails are delivered

steps.action: Measure the delivery latency against a pre-change baseline
steps.expected: No material regression from the added conversion work
